scope_note: Initial direct-evidence discovery and distinct gap-closure audit for the 143,439-square-foot IM3 Microsoft building footprint in Quincy, Grant County. Coordinate, assessor, SEPA and air-permit evidence place the footprint in Microsoft's MWH (formerly Project Oxford) campus at 1515 Port Industrial Way, not the separate Columbia campus at 501 Port Industrial Parkway that opened in 2007. Campus real- and personal-property accounts, a mixed-campus power-facilities agreement, MWH equipment, regional impact claims and supporting water infrastructure remain explicitly unallocated; no public record crosswalks the footprint to an MWH building code, tax-account share, employee roster, contract value or utility meter.

sources.title: Growing with the cloud—Quincy, WA
sources.notes: The operator describes two Quincy campuses with more than 20 buildings and about 2 million square feet. These current portfolio descriptors cannot identify the selected IM3 footprint or backdate it to the original 2007 Columbia opening.

sources.title: Grant County property account 72793 — parcel 313769000
sources.notes: The official portal identifies Microsoft Corporation real-property account 72793 at 1515 NW Port Industrial Parkway, parcel 313769000, with 152.91 acres, multiple separately dated improvements and annual value/tax history. The account is campus-wide; its several 140,908-square-foot improvements do not match or crosswalk the selected 143,439-square-foot IM3 polygon. Taxable and appraised value are equal in the retained years and exemption loss is displayed as zero, which does not address state sales/use-tax preferences.

sources.title: Grant County personal-property account 84139 — Microsoft MWH
sources.notes: The official portal labels personal-property account 84139 'MWH - 1515 NW Port Industrial Pkwy' and supplies annual value and payment history. It is kept separate from real account 72793 and from later MWH20/MWH21/MWH23/MWH30 personal accounts at M Street addresses. The 2026 personal-property bill was only partly paid when reviewed and is not retained.

sources.title: Microsoft MWH Approval Order 22AQ-E035 and technical support document
sources.notes: The current order identifies the MWH facility at 1515 Port Industrial Parkway and lists commissioning dates from 2015 through 2022. Its equipment tables contain 45 generators for MWH01/02 and 72 for MWH03/04/05/06, 117 total. Permit equipment and potential-emissions limits are not actual generation, runtime, fuel use or emissions.

sources.title: SEPA 201805050 — MWH03-04-05-06 Microsoft Data Center
sources.notes: The register describes approximately 950,000 square feet of phased MWH03-06 construction on about 212 acres at 1500 Port Industrial Parkway and an increase from 1.4 million to 1.6 million square feet on the Microsoft campus. These are proposal/campus figures, not a final selected-building area, spend or completion date.

sources.title: SEPA 202403581 — MWH08 Data Center
sources.notes: The register identifies a later proposed 455,000-square-foot, two-story MWH08 building at 1515 Port Industrial Way on parcel 042009305. It is evidence of continuing campus expansion and is excluded from the selected footprint and the older parcel account.

sources.title: JLARC Final Report 17-02 — Data Center Equipment sales and use tax preference
sources.publisher: Washington State Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee
sources.notes: The review names Microsoft Corporation among statewide direct beneficiaries and reports that 12 of 15 beneficiaries through 2014 were in Grant County. It also explains that reporting defects prevent direct beneficiary-savings measurement. Aggregate savings, job requirements, REMI multipliers and fiscal scenarios cannot be assigned to MWH or the selected building.

sources.title: Grant PUD January 25, 2022 FYI packet — December 2021 contracts
sources.notes: The contract register reports a $4,807,473 awarded amount in parentheses for Microsoft Large Power Facilities Agreement 140-10532, covering Columbia CO5 and MWH3&4, executed December 7, 2021 with an August 7, 2023 completion date. Later registers still showed it open. Parentheses are consistent with a PUD receivable, but the register is not a payment ledger; the amount is retained only as a mixed-campus source projection.

sources.title: Microsoft and City of Quincy water supply and facility agreement with Addendum 2
sources.notes: The agreement distinguishes the Columbia facility from Project Oxford/MWH, defines Oxford phases and water rights, and anticipates approximately $10,469,601.82 for Oxford utility infrastructure subject to final design and bid cost. Its $62,728.85 monthly payment is expressly illustrative. Neither figure is normalized because the former may be nested in the later $31 million reuse-system record and the latter is not an actual bill.

sources.title: City of Quincy financial statements audit report, 2020-2021
sources.notes: The audit says Microsoft-completed reuse components and City-completed components coexist, while City financing is backed by Microsoft and repaid through rates. Fund and debt schedules are City-wide or project-wide and cannot be assigned to the selected building; they are not added to the existing $31 million EPA total.

sources.title: Economic contributions of Microsoft's data centers in the Central Washington region
sources.notes: The factsheet reports 377 Microsoft jobs in 2024, $2 million of FY2019-2024 community investment and $26.4 million of 2024 property taxes, but its scope spans Chelan, Douglas and Grant counties. It mixes onsite contractors with modeled indirect/induced jobs and labels construction jobs, labor income and regional GDP as impacts. Those broader and modeled figures are not converted into selected-building observations.

sources.title: Microsoft gifts $25K to BBCC Data Center Program
sources.notes: The public-college recipient confirms a $25,000 Microsoft Community Empowerment Fund gift for Data Center Academy scholarships. It is a Grant County community record but is not allocated to MWH or the selected footprint and may be nested in a broader operator total.

sources.title: Commission recap 6-11-2019 — Microsoft conservation rebate
sources.notes: The PUD says Microsoft forwent a conservation rebate, allowing $480,000 to be dispersed through a Pay-it-Forward program, and separately discusses systemwide Quincy transmission expansion. The recap does not identify the contributing campus, selected building, recipient payments or marginal service costs, so no amount is assigned here.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — project boundary and chronology corrected
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 coordinates/footprint, Microsoft releases, Grant County assessor address/owner search, Ecology SEPA and current/rescinded air orders, City agreements and parcel identifiers. Queries/identifiers: Microsoft, Quincy, MWH, Oxford, Columbia, 1515/1500/501 Port Industrial, parcel 313769000, IM3 00499403180, MWH01-MWH08, CO1-CO9; 2007-2026. Result: useful boundary correction. The selected 143,439-square-foot polygon lies in MWH, where permits show construction/commissioning from 2014/2015 through 2022, not the separate Columbia campus that opened in 2007. MWH08 and M Street expansions are later/outside assets. No source crosswalks this polygon to an MWH code; 2007 is rejected as selected-building treatment timing.
project_updates.project_description: Microsoft Quincy is the Microsoft-operated MWH data-center campus at 1515 Port Industrial Way in Quincy, Grant County, Washington; the selected project is one 143,439-square-foot IM3-mapped building footprint within that campus, not the separate Columbia campus at 501 Port Industrial Parkway or Microsoft's broader Central Washington portfolio. County assessor improvements and state Ecology records show MWH construction and commissioning in phases from 2014/2015 through 2022, while the exact mapped footprint cannot be crosswalked to an MWH building code. Later MWH08 and M Street expansions, tenant equipment, and off-site utility infrastructure remain outside the individual-building boundary unless expressly retained as unallocated context.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — real-property fiscal account
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Grant County Assessor/Treasurer owner, parcel, value, improvement, statement and payment pages. Query/identifier: owner Microsoft; account 72793; parcel 313769000; 1515 NW Port Industrial Parkway; tax/appraisal years 2014-2026. Result: useful. Eight positive annual appraised-value stocks and five fully paid real-property tax statements are retained. The portal's owner query returned ten distinct Microsoft real/personal accounts, including separate Columbia, MWH, M Street and Road S properties. The account is campus-wide, so it is not divided by footprint or improvement count; appraised value is not investment, and payment is not net fiscal benefit.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — personal-property fiscal account
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: the same official owner search and the MWH-labeled personal-property detail/payment pages. Query/identifier: account 84139, geo ID 4830750, MWH, 1515 NW Port Industrial Parkway; tax/appraisal years 2017-2026. Result: useful. Eight annual appraised-value stocks and four fully paid tax statements are retained separately from real property. Later MWH20/MWH21/MWH23/MWH30 accounts 84863/84864 and a partially paid 2026 bill are excluded. No server/equipment inventory or building allocation is inferred.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — air permit and commissioning chronology
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Ecology data-center orders, technical support documents, current/rescinded permit index and facility-history sections. Query/identifier: A0250310, 22AQ-E035, 20AQ-E005, 19AQ-E031, 18AQ-E024, 14AQ-E537, MWH01-MWH06; 2014-2022. Result: useful. The current order supports 117 permit-listed generators and unit-level commissioning from September 2015 through June 2022. Permit quantities and potential-emission scenarios are retained only as authorization/equipment evidence; actual kWh, run hours, fuel, emissions, damages and selected-building equipment remain unknown.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — planning, building and site-development records
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Ecology SEPA register/checklists, City of Quincy planning/council archives, parcel/address search and construction-stormwater facilities. Queries/identifiers: 201805050, SEPA 2024-008/202403581, WAR313961, MWH03-08, MWH90, parcel 313769000/042009305; 2013-2026. Result: boundary and proposal facts only. SEPA reports about 950,000 square feet of phased MWH03-06 work and later 455,000-square-foot MWH08, but no issued-building-permit value, final cost, certificate date, selected-footprint crosswalk, contractor payments, worker hours or local purchasing. Proposed areas are not relabeled as operating area.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — incentives, compliance and public-cost audit
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Washington JLARC tax-preference review, DOR rural-data-center eligibility/notices/performance-report forms, State Auditor and City financial records. Queries/identifiers: Microsoft, MWH, Oxford, parcel 313769000, data center sales/use exemption, certificate, beneficiary savings, jobs, clawback, grant, loan, refund, abatement; 2010-2026. Result: material negative. Microsoft is a named beneficiary, but company/facility certificates, savings, exempt purchases, job-compliance results and clawbacks are confidential or aggregated. Assessor exemption loss is zero only for local property accounts. No selected-building incentive, public grant, marginal police/fire/road/administrative cost or same-scope fiscal net was found; statewide REMI/fiscal scenarios are rejected.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — electricity and transmission account
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Grant PUD contract registers/FYI packets, rate schedules, data-center FAQ, commission recaps, load-growth/transmission materials and customer limits. Queries/identifiers: Microsoft, MWH3&4, CO5, 140-10532, QTEP, large power, load, meter, rate, rebate, facilities agreement; 2011-2026. Result: one mixed-campus source projection retained. The $4,807,473 award is not treated as a paid amount. No selected-building service capacity, peak demand, tariff class, kWh, bill, payment, PUD capital cost or reimbursement exists publicly; systemwide Quincy transmission estimates and queue MW are not customer allocations.

project_updates.title: Direct discovery — water and wastewater account
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: City-Microsoft water supply/facility agreements and exhibits, City audits, EPA reuse case study, Ecology water rights/industrial permits and current operator water claims. Queries/identifiers: Project Oxford, MWH, Columbia, IRWTP/QRWU, QB 206(D), QB 1547, cooling effluent, rate, capital cost, meter, gallons; 2011-2026. Result: the existing $31 million reuse-system actual remains the authoritative broad infrastructure record. The 2014 approximately $10,469,601.82 Oxford estimate and illustrative $62,728.85 monthly payment are excluded as overlapping/planning examples. No selected-building metered withdrawal, consumption, discharge, rate payment or public subsidy was found.

project_updates.title: Gap closure — city accounting and infrastructure incidence
project_updates.notes: Distinct gap-closure pass after direct discovery. Source families checked: 2020-2021 audited statements, reuse construction funds, debt/liability schedules, completed-scope note and rate-incidence language. Queries/identifiers: Microsoft, reuse, Oxford, MWH, Fund 460, capital upgrades, loan, bond, guarantee, rate, expenditure. Result: useful scope reconciliation but no new record. Microsoft and City completed different components; City debt/funds cover wider works and Microsoft-backed rate recovery. Components, debt totals, the Oxford estimate and the $31 million EPA project total are not summed because timing, nesting and economic incidence differ.

project_updates.title: Gap closure — operations, payroll and impact-report audit
project_updates.notes: Distinct gap-closure pass. Source families checked: Microsoft Central Washington impact factsheet, current Washington factsheets, Quincy/Central Washington workforce pages and live job descriptions; BLS/QCEW and Census/CBP context. Queries/identifiers: Quincy, MWH, employee, contractor, security, technician, payroll, wage, residence, Datacenter Academy; 2014-2026. Result: no selected-building operating observation. The 377 jobs and $93,000 average compensation are three-county portfolio figures; 287 onsite contractors are embedded in a larger modeled total. Job postings are vacancies. No building/campus headcount, payroll, employee residence, retention or realized training-to-hire total is retained.

project_updates.title: Gap closure — construction workforce and suppliers
project_updates.notes: Distinct gap-closure pass. Source families checked: SEPA attachments, permit contractor fields, operator releases, contractor/project pages, PUD contract registers, federal procurement indexes and City/Port records. Queries/identifiers: MWH01-MWH08, Oxford, Turner, Hoffman, contractor, subcontractor, vendor, invoice, award, payroll, labor hours, local spend; 2014-2026. Result: later construction is identifiable, but no selected-building contractor roster, private contract/payment, worker count, hours, payroll, supplier address at payment time or Grant County retained purchase share was found. No supplier, construction-job-year or local-spend model is eligible.

project_updates.title: Gap closure — community and recipient confirmation
project_updates.notes: Distinct gap-closure pass. Source families checked: Microsoft community pages, Big Bend Community College/Foundation board packets and scholarship pages, Quincy schools, Columbia Basin Foundation, ChangeX and Grant PUD recipient/payment materials. Queries/identifiers: Microsoft, Quincy, MWH, gift, grant, scholarship, donation, microgrant, Pay-it-Forward; 2014-2026. Result: the recipient-confirmed $25,000 BBCC gift is retained. A $30,000 annual scholarship description, later $60,000 plan, $480,000 foregone-rebate program and $2 million three-county operator total have uncertain period, allocation or nesting and are not combined. No selected-building community transfer exists.

project_updates.title: Gap closure — fiscal reconciliation and material negatives
project_updates.notes: Distinct gap-closure pass. Source families checked: PUD rebate/contract records, County property accounts, City financial/audit indexes, state incentive material, SEC filings and municipal debt/bond searches. Queries/identifiers: Microsoft/MWH/Oxford/Quincy, account 72793/84139, tax bill, payment, refund, check register, service cost, bond, TIF, IRB, lien and litigation; 2014-2026. Result: real and personal tax accounts are compatible only as separate series and are not automatically summed. The $26.4 million regional tax total overlaps local accounts; the $480,000 foregone rebate lacks campus attribution; the PUD agreement lacks payment evidence. No incentive amount, public-service cost, net fiscal result, judgment or recovery is retained.

project_updates.title: Adversarial continuation — metric and model disposition ledger
project_updates.notes: Initial pass record disposition: Investment — retain the existing $31 million city-owned reuse infrastructure actual at supporting-infrastructure scope; retain the $4,807,473 mixed-campus PUD agreement only as a source projection; reject assessed value, the overlapping Oxford estimate and broader regional claims as investment. Construction — rejected: no selected-building permit value, expenditure, workers, hours or payroll. Operations — rejected: no selected-building/campus realized employees, payroll or revenue; regional jobs/wages are unallocated. Suppliers — rejected: no payment, vendor-location or local-retention bounds. Fiscal — retain separate campus real/personal assessed values and paid-tax series; reject regional overlapping tax totals, selected-building allocation, incentive value and netting. Public costs — rejected: no same-scope marginal service, infrastructure, debt-service or administrative cost. Community — retain the unallocated recipient-confirmed $25,000 gift; reject allocation and aggregation with broader totals. Resources — retain 117 campus permit-listed generators; reject actual generator use/emissions and selected-building electricity/water/waste observations. County employment — causal and descriptive models rejected because the corrected MWH treatment is phased/unknown at building level, Columbia predates it and multiple operators/concurrent expansions confound attribution. County wages — rejected for the same timing/counterfactual defects and no worker-residence bridge. County GDP — rejected for the same defects; Microsoft's $269 million figure is a source-reported regional impact, not an observed project contribution. Last-resort models considered and rejected: assessor-value-to-investment conversion, tax-share allocation by floor area, tax-equal public-cost break-even, utility capacity/annual-use conversion, generator capacity/runtime, construction job-years/payroll, supplier multiplier, community proxy, and county comparison gaps. Each lacks a necessary direct anchor or non-overlap proof; modeled additions: zero. Handoff remains candidate_pending_adversarial_review; this initial discovery-plus-gap-closure account is provisional and never accepted. No records requests were made.
